summary: WAYLOAM v0.4.4.alpha fixes long-distance expedition-stop discovery so camps, water, food and bike services follow the real bicycle corridor instead of sparse straight-line approximations.
highlights: Long routes now use distance-aware POI corridor sampling instead of collapsing the whole trip to 48 geometry points.
A roughly 1,668 km route keeps hundreds of corridor samples, preventing winding sections from losing nearby camps and services.
Overpass discovery runs in overlapping chunks with multiple public endpoint fallbacks and a wider route-matching tolerance.
A long route that returns zero usable POIs is surfaced as a retryable enrichment failure instead of silently becoming one giant stage.
added: Regression coverage for continent-scale POI corridor density and maximum sample gaps.
A third public Overpass fallback endpoint for expedition-stop discovery.
Explicit long-route empty-result validation so zero markers cannot masquerade as valid data.
changed: POI corridor samples are spaced by travelled distance along the actual route rather than by raw geometry index.
Expedition POI discovery retains up to 2,500 route services instead of truncating long trips to the first 400 results.
POI queries use overlapping route chunks with limited concurrency so long trips remain practical without flooding public OSM services.
The enrichment service is now focused only on elevation and expedition services; primary bicycle routing remains fully embedded and local.
fixed: Fixed long winding routes losing nearly every camp, water point and shop because sparse query chords drifted away from the real bicycle route.
Fixed successful-but-empty Overpass responses silently producing a 1,000+ km single stage with no markers.
Fixed the long-route POI cap disproportionately keeping only early-trip services and starving later stages of overnight stops.
